content:
gareth: Heads-up — scheduling a 90m maintenance window for Dedicated GPU pool (eu-west) to roll kernel + pin model variant. Tentative start: 2026-04-02 00:00 UTC. Will post statuspage + customer email once copy is approved. tagging @support_lead @marketing_ops

emily: Thanks. Can you include expected customer impact (latency / availability) and rollback criteria? Support needs exact wording for statuspage snippet.

deploybot: deploybot: scheduled job queued. Plan: canary 2/10 at +5m, stagger 10m batches, monitoring hooks for error rate, 95th-latency, and KV cache miss rate. Auto-pause on thresholds. I will post events here.

support_lead: Draft statuspage snippet below — please review quickly: ```Status: Maintenance in progress. We are performing a scheduled update to our Dedicated GPU pool in eu-west. During the window some requests may see transient latency increases (up to ~30s) or short-lived errors while instances are cycled. We expect normal service to resume after the window. Impact: transient latency spikes or <1% error rate for a limited set of requests. ETA: 2026-04-02 00:00 UTC - 01:30 UTC.```

support_lead: Draft customer e-mail (short): "We will perform a maintenance update for Dedicated GPU instances in eu-west on 2026-04-02 00:00 UTC for ~90 minutes. Some requests may experience brief latency increases or retries. No customer action required. Contact support if you observe persistent errors."

alice: nit: change "up to ~30s" to "brief retries or short latency spikes (seconds)" — ops prefers not to promise exact max seconds. Also call out fallback model pin for Private deployments if applicable.

marketing_ops: LGTM otherwise. Suggest subject: "Planned maintenance: Dedicated GPU pool (eu-west) — Apr 2" and add CTA link to support portal.

dan: Ops-runbook / rollback criteria proposal: rollback and abort rollout if any of the following during a staged batch: 1) sustained 95th percentile latency increase >200ms for 3 consecutive minutes, 2) error rate >1.0% for 5 minutes, or 3) KV cache miss rate spike >5x baseline causing token-per-request surge. If triggered, deploybot will pin previous model and restore routing.

ops_oncall: I'll be on standby for the window. Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/dedicated-kernel-roll — I have playbook open.

deploybot: Canary batch started at 00:05 UTC — canary nodes 2/10. Monitoring hooks enabled.

deploybot: Canary alert at 00:12 UTC — error rate 0.8% (threshold 0.5%). Pausing rollout automatically and keeping canary pinned to previous image. Logs: ```[canary] 00:12:07 ERR 0.8% errors, spike in redis timeout on model kv-cache```.

gareth: Decision: abort this rollout. Rollback canary -> previous pinned model. Support, please draft a brief customer update referencing the pause and next steps; marketing, prepare an updated send but hold for ops confirmation.

support_lead: Customer update draft: "Update: During a scheduled maintenance attempt we observed elevated error rates on a canary subset in eu-west. We paused the rollout and reverted the canary to the prior configuration. No action required. We are investigating root cause and will publish a new maintenance date. Apologies for the interruption."

marketing_ops: Updated subject line to: "Maintenance attempt paused — Dedicated GPU pool (eu-west)". Added support CTA and link to status page.

alice: :thumbsup: good call to pause. Suggest we schedule next attempt in a lower-traffic window and add extra preflight smoke tests.

deploybot: rollback completed at 00:20 UTC. All canary nodes restored to prior model and kernel. Final state: stable. Events saved to /deploys/3876543210/events.json

gareth: Thanks everyone. Next actions: ops to root-cause, support to publish the statuspage update (use draft snippet above), marketing to queue customer email but hold send until RCA available. We'll reconvene tomorrow 09:30 UTC to plan the next window.
